:''For the tournament, see [[1996 Decipher World Championship]].''

'''Star Wars World Championships''' is a special report by [[Michael Mikaelian]] in ''[[InQuest]]'' #22 (February 1997, page 14). Mikaelian wrote it after playing the [[1996 Decipher World Championship]] at the Vail Cascade Hotel and Club in Vail, Colorado.<ref name="inquest">Michael Mikaelian, "Star Wars World Championships", ''InQuest'' #22 (February 1997), p. 14. Scan: [https://archive.org/details/inquest-magazine-issue-22 InQuest Magazine Issue 22], Internet Archive.</ref>

[[File:InQuest 22 page 14.jpg|thumb|right|260px|InQuest #22, February 1997, page 14.]]

The issue identified Mikaelian as of Brooklyn, New York, and as the author of InQuest #20's Killer Decks II Yavin 4 Counterstrike deck. He qualified for the championships of 7–9 December 1996. He filed the report after the trip home.<ref name="inquest" />

== Photograph ==

[[File:Michael Mikaelian at 1996 Worlds table.jpg|thumb|right|320px|[[Michael Mikaelian]] at the 1996 World Championship. Photo: Decipher.]]

The still is printed "Photo courtesy of Decipher." The magazine caption names Mikaelian at the Star Wars worlds.<ref name="inquest" />

== Arrival ==

Mikaelian opened: "It was snowing when I arrived on Hoth."<ref name="inquest" />

He wrote that most people think of Colorado as "well, Colorado." For Decipher, Colorado was "the ice world of Hoth from George Lucas' \"Star Wars.\""<ref name="inquest" />

Thirteen of the 38 competitors were stranded on the road for five hours. Safety workers ran avalanche control above Vail Pass, the only road between Denver and Vail. Wintry weather the Friday night before the tournament did not stop anyone from arriving.<ref name="inquest" />

== Saturday ==

The championships began Saturday morning with two-player matches. Mikaelian wrote that many of the world's top 20 Star Wars CCG players were there.<ref name="inquest" />

His first-round opponent was [[Joe Alread]], whom he had defeated in the finals of the [[1996 GenCon Open]]. Alread's X-wings used [[A Few Maneuvers]]. Mikaelian wrote that every time they battled, he lost half of his forces. Alread won by three Force, "thus avenging his earlier loss to me."<ref name="inquest" />

After each match, point totals and Force differentials were totaled. A win scored two points, a tie one, and a loss none. Each player then received a new opponent with similar ratings.<ref name="inquest" />

Mikaelian wrote that play was friendly. Players wished one another luck before each game and congratulated opponents afterward.<ref name="inquest" />

His second opponent was [[Rusty Zion]]. Zion tried to block Mikaelian's Force drains. Mikaelian's [[Jawa|Jawas]] beat Zion's spies. He then "surprised the Empire by hitching a few rides with [[Nabrun Leids]]" and used [[Sorry About The Mess]] with [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] for a five-card win.<ref name="inquest" />

When Saturday ended, Mikaelian's earlier opponents had made the top 12. Alread ranked first. Mikaelian finished 29th.<ref name="inquest" />

== Sunday ==

Sunday started at 9 a.m. with random pairings among the twelve. The championship match was [[Bjørn Sørgjerd]] of Norway against [[Raphael Asselin]] of Canada.<ref name="inquest" />

=== Game one ===

Sørgjerd played Dark Side. He used [[Darth Vader]] and [[Grand Moff Tarkin]] on Tatooine, with [[Mosep]], against Asselin's all-space Light deck. Asselin discarded Obi-Wan Kenobi from the top of his deck. Sørgjerd won by nine cards.<ref name="inquest" />

=== Game two ===

Asselin played Dark Side. He deployed a fleet of [[Imperial-Class Star Destroyer|Imperial Star Destroyers]] and used [[Scanning Crew]] to look at Sørgjerd's hand. Asselin's ships drained Sørgjerd's Force at every system. Sørgjerd's attempt to control the surface of Tatooine was crushed by the Star Destroyers.<ref name="inquest" />

The [[Millennium Falcon]] was destroyed with all hands aboard, including [[Han Solo]]. Sørgjerd said, "It is a dark time for the Rebellion."<ref name="inquest" />

=== Tie-breaker ===

Sørgjerd saw that Asselin would win, and that the championship would come down to a two-game Force-differential tie-breaker. He tried to reduce Asselin's Force to nine or less. When the Light Side succumbed, Asselin had enough Force to claim the championship.<ref name="inquest" />

== Prize ==

Asselin's prize was a plaque and an all-expenses-paid trip to Tunisia. The trip included the remnants of George Lucas's Mos Eisley Cantina and Lars homestead film sets from the original ''Star Wars''.<ref name="inquest" />

Asselin won the championship. Sørgjerd was runner-up. After Saturday, Asselin sat third and Sørgjerd ninth.<ref name="inquest" />
